submission.natural_language_explanation: Context-free piece detector: the pole's strength is a pure function of the current vocabulary piece - identical (spread 0.000) at every occurrence of a piece in the scan and reproduced exactly when the same pieces are run in a synthetic context - and it fires on a graded, lexically specific learned lexicon of 'putting forth' vocabulary: the express family (express 1.41 = the pole's max, expresses, expressed, expressing, expression, expressions, expressive), develop/develops/developed/developing/development/developmental, deliver/delivers/delivered/delivering, build/builds/built, integrate/integrates/integrated/integrating, implement/implemented/implementing, combine/combines/combined/combining, communicate/communicated/communicating/communication, convey/conveyed/conveying, publish/published/publishing, release/releases/released/releasing, write/writing/written, teach/teaches/taught/teaching, educate/educational, demonstrate/demonstrates/demonstrated, illustrate/illustrating, depicts/depicting, showcase, propagate, formulated, synthesized, crafted, mold/molded, produce/produced/producing, accumulate/accumulated, validate/validated, evaluate/evaluates/evaluating, constructed/constructing, compose/composed, incorporate/incorporates, contain/contains/contained/containing, include/includes/included/including, focuses/focused, reflect/reflects, adopt/adopted, enhances/enhanced, plus a piece-specific technical/scalar tail (pure 0.80, dense, thick, broad, severe, acute, intense, strong, strict, subtle, profound, portable, powerful, formal, pragmatic, explicit, effective, functional, aerobic, acoustic, poetic, coherent, elegant, compact, absolute, concise, dose/doses/dosage, polyethylene, ethylene, ethoxy, fecal, and fragments such as ' ureth' 1.27, 'crete' 1.09, 'phy', 'Con'); it is piece-specific, not semantic or morphological: same-meaning pieces sit at the floor (describe 0.13, state -0.14, say -0.17, tell -0.04, explain -0.04, report 0.03, reveal 0.04, declare -0.10, voice 0.00, create 0.15, make -0.09, form 0.07, shape 0.06, invent -0.09), so do the missing inflections of firing stems (building 0.14, buildings -0.09, writes 0.02, wrote 0.08, education 0.11, educated 0.08, teacher 0.07, delivery 0.23, combination 0.12, implementation 0.07, publication 0.08, developments 0.06, developer 0.30), entity/topic nouns (protein -0.09, enzyme 0.11, buffer -0.17, genome -0.15, sample -0.14, study -0.04, method -0.11, analysis -0.15) and -ation nouns (qualification, compensation, interpretation, regulation, information, all at the -0.17 floor), while the piece fires at full strength in every sense or part of speech ('the express train' 1.41, 'the express lane' 1.41, 'the math expression' 0.89) and the sentence-initial unspaced form is a distinct, weaker piece ('Express' 0.54); the class is graded (2,210 of the 50,304 pieces reach 0.25 of max, 772 reach 0.5, 149 reach 0.7, and 887 sit at the GELU floor of -0.17), so a new text is predicted active when it contains any piece of the firing lexicon in any context and inactive otherwise.

rival_explanations: Semantic-class reading: the pole detects the meaning 'to put something into words or bring it into being', so every near-synonym (create, make, form, say, tell, describe, explain, state, reveal, voice) should fire as strongly as express and develop, and the odd pieces (dose, ureth, fecal, dfrac) are scan noise.

Morphological-family reading: the pole fires on every inflected form and derivative of the roughly forty firing stems, so building, buildings, writes, wrote, education, educated, teacher, delivery, combination, implementation, publication, developments and developer should fire too, and no piece outside those families should.

Syntactic-frame reading: the pole detects the to-infinitive verb slot that every top example sits in ('to express', 'to develop', 'can deliver'), so 'develop' should fire after 'to' but not in 'a development', and the to-infinitives of silent verbs (to measure, to analyse, to characterize) should fire while the same words elsewhere do not.

top_examples.text:
In my idea, deep learning is a process of feature extraction.
Just like multiple layer neural networks (NN):
Input1 => L1 => L2 => ... => Ln => Output1. The special aspect of deep learning is to let
Output1 equal to
Input1. As a result, we can get the error of
Output1. Then, we can try to use backpropagation (BP) to train our model to minimize the error. When it is complete, all layers' output is the internal feature representations from edge to partial of object to full object. This made deep learning so fancy. This concept is illustrated by this picture:
Now, back to convolutional neural networks (CNN). CNN use convolution to extract features and try to learn all filters by BP. I do not see CNN generate the output similar to the input pictures. It is just convolution and pooling and so on to become very small pixel fractions, called basis.
How CNN use deep learning concept in its implementation? Why BP can train CNN model to the correct internal features of all layers?
Deep learning is a generic term that refers to the fact that a deep neural network has at least one hidden layer.
First, mind that deep learning is a buzz term. There is not even a consensus of a formal definition in the research community. A discussion of the term does not lead anywhere, really. It's just a word.
That being said, convolutional nets are deep because they rely on multiple layers of feature extraction, as you said. They extract features from the input to predict an outcome.
What you refer to is a "generative" approach, i.e. the features are used to create the observation (a picture, not a class label). That is what made deep learning popular, but it is in no way limited to that.
The deep learning is an approach where you have a lot of relatively simple layers. You increase learning capabilities by increasing the number of layers, as opposed to increased complexity of layers. You could for instance come up with very fancy output functions, maybe nonlinear functions of inputs or complicated connections. Instead you stick with simple things like ReLU and liner combination and softmax, but stack a lot of layers one on top of other. That's why CNN perfectly fits into this very generic and rather vague definition of deep learning. Look at CNN's components, they are usually very simple MAX, convolutions etc.

The five states that were impacted by the Deepwater Horizon disaster (including 665 miles of contaminated coastline), Gulf Coast business owners, the federal government and BP have spent the past three years dancing a slow legal tango that has assessed clean-up costs, fines and other liabilities.
The British oil giant estimates its overall liability for the catastrophe could eventually top $42 billion; BP has sold off significant assets to generate cash for the payouts.
In December, a federal judge approved the Deepwater Horizon Economic and Property Damages Settlement agreement, which covers individuals and businesses in Louisiana, Mississippi, Alabama, and certain coastal counties in eastern Texas and western Florida, as well as specified adjacent Gulf waters and bays. BP says it has set aside about $8 billion to cover these economic and property damage loss claims (the agreement does not set a cap on the liability), of which about $1.87 billion has already been paid out (the overall settlement includes a guaranteed $2.3-billion fund to compensate seafood industry businesses damaged by the spill).
Meanwhile, a trial underway in New Orleans will determine civil claims under the Clean Water Act which could amount to more than $17 billion; billions more could be assessed after damage claims from Gulf Coast states are adjudicated; and a third set of claims covering natural resource damage has yet to be filed.
While the overall scope of the settlements is still taking shape, a bureaucratic framework has been put in place to distribute these funds.
In 2011, the RESTORE Act established a Gulf Coast Ecosystem Restoration Council, which is comprised of governors from the five affected States, the Secretaries from the U.S. Departments of the Interior, Commerce, Agriculture, and Homeland Security as well as the Secretary of the Army and the Administrator of the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency. The Gulf States recommended and President Obama appointed the Secretary of Commerce as the Council’s Chair.

If you are reading this blog on a handheld mobile device or on a laptop, stop what you are doing and make sure that your neck and spine are positioned at a natural, comfortable angle to avoid a spinal cord injury in the making.
The SFGate reports that more doctors are documenting cases of spinal cord injuries dubbed “Blackberry Neck” that are caused by the positions we put our bodies in so that we can use mobile phones and portable computers. In fact, it is getting so bad that pretty soon doctors are going to develop a separate type of paralysis treatment to help fix the damage we do to our neck and spine using everyday electronics.
The spinal cord injury lawyers at our San Diego law firm are always concerned about the use handheld mobile devices for drivers out on the road, because they distract drivers and cause car accidents that lead to paralysis. But now they might be doing significant damage to your neck and back, little-by-little, without you even realizing it.
A Kaiser Permanente sports medicine specialist was quote as saying “…we have a much more sedentary lifestyle, and much more computer interfacing with laptops and PDAs and cell phones. We see a lot of poor posturing, a lot of stress on the wrists.”
These injuries are not as dangerous as a shattered spinal column or spondylolisthesis, but damage is done over time and it will only get worse as technology gets better. Several weeks ago, Apple announced their new product called the iPad, which is sleek and cool, but will it add to this epidemic? What is Apple doing to make sure that their product does not put strain on the necks and backs of their customers?
In general, staring at an electronic screen or using a keyboard for typing can have a negative impact on your body’s health. With laptops, cell phones, and iPods, we typically hold them at a lower angle, forcing us to strain our necks in order to see the screen, giving us “Blackberry Neck” from maintaining bad posture.
So what can be done? Our paralysis attorneys have the following suggestions for how to reduce “Blackberry Neck” symptoms when using handheld mobile devices:
- Take a Break: Been on the laptop for a while? Staring at your cell phone for a few hours? Put down the technology and give yourself a breather.
- Take a Walk: It is good to readjust your body’s position every 20-30 minutes to make sure it does not put too much weight and pressure on one area for too long. Get up and move around! Even just a little bit can help.
- Take Support: Find a way to support yourself, using your body (for example, your elbows) to bring the screen of your device closer to your head or buy a supplementary item for your device that does not sacrifice your posture while you work.

This analysis looks behind the scenes at how the ban on offshore drilling was lifted and what that had to do with the ultimate prize for big oil, the American Power Act. It focuses on the current administration. That in no way implies that the problem originated in January 2009. The out sized and destructive influence of the oil monopoly has been with us for since the 1870's.
Banning Offshore Drilling
In 1969 a Unocal oil rig off the coast of Santa Barbara, California began leaking oil. The extent of the leak, damage to wildlife, and the shoreline caused considerable outrage. The state of California banned offshore drilling shortly after the leak. In 1980, Congress banned offshore drilling in most federally controlled waters. President George H.W. Bush reluctantly banned off shore drilling in 1990 for California, Florida, Oregon and Washington and in the North Atlantic.
Lifting that ban has been a top priority for oil companies in the United States. In 2006, the U.S. House of Representatives voted to lift the ban on offshore drilling for 85% of the nation's shoreline. The Senate failed to cooperate. Just before leaving office, President George W. Bush lifted the executive order banning offshore drilling and challenged Congress to complete the process with legislation. No action was taken.
It took a Democratic President to change the decade's long policy. On March 31, President Obama lifted the ban on offshore drilling covering 85% of the nation's shoreline. The Gulf of Mexico coastline, location of the BP catastrophe, had not been included in the original ban.
Obama's Very Bad Timing
The president had the worst timing imaginable for this announcement. Just 22 days later, BP's Deepwater Horizon rig off the Louisiana coast failed miserably and has been leaking ever since. Obama's remarks at the March 31 announcement came back to haunt him even though the offshore drilling by BP and the others in the Gulf of Mexico had been in place for years.
Obama stressed that great care would be taken to protect the environment.
"So today we’re announcing the expansion of offshore oil and gas exploration, but in ways that balance the need to harness domestic energy resources and the need to protect America’s natural resources. Under the leadership of Secretary Salazar, we’ll employ new technologies that reduce the impact of oil exploration. Iron Cross Symbolism & Meanings
As time goes on styles change, and so does symbolism and meanings of certain symbols. At times, a symbol can have negative meanings, and at other times it the same symbol can be seen as a positive thing. If you are going to be getting a tattoo of any kind, it is always important to know the history behind the art or symbol.
You could get a tattoo thinking it’s a wonderful thing, and then find out too late that it actually means something totally different. Plus, knowing the history behind your tattoo can make it all the more interesting. It’s definitely a great way to break the ice with new people. This article will discuss the varied history of the iron cross as well as its symbolism so that you can have a better understanding of this common tattoo.
When many people think of a cross they think of a shape that is much like a lower case “T.” The iron cross shares this basic style, but instead of having some limbs of the “T” longer or shorter than each other, all of the limbs of the cross are the same length. It looks much more like a rotated “X” than a “T.” The iron cross also has just about nothing to do with Jesus of Nazareth as well. This symbol has been a decoration or honor in armies since the early 1800’s, not a symbol for Christ.
History Of The Iron Cross Symbol
It is said that the iron cross was designed by a man named Karl Friedrich. The design was then introduced as a sort of medal of honor for acts of bravery and leadership by Kaiser Frederic Wilhelm in 1813. This was not the only time that the iron cross was used as an honor is wars, though. It was again used in the Franco-Prussian war in 1870. Again, this doesn’t end the symbol’s war history.
A good symbol tends to be reused through time, and this was true of the iron cross, which was again used during World War I. The iron cross was only used in one war after that, in World War II when Hitler used it to reward soldiers in his army. His iron cross was slightly different, with a swastika in the middle of it. This part of the symbol’s history tainted the symbol in war, and it has not been used as a medal of honor since.
Iron Cross Symbolic Meanings
While the iron cross is no longer used for war, it is used for one thing in particular, bikers. Bikers, or people who take great pride in riding motorcycles, still use this symbol. However, they do not relate it to Hitler, or any other war leader. They see it as the proud symbol that it once was.
The medal once symbolized honor, loyalty, bravery, faith, and courage. The sign of the iron cross still symbolizes all of these things. It is no longer seen as the negative sign that it was during the second world war. While it is a symbol that mostly bikers get tattooed on themselves, it would be okay for anyone to get this tattoo, so long as they relate to the great symbolism in it.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: In the first section the author describes how the team measured the flow of water through the filter. The next section explains the method and gives the results for each trial.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Explicit floor near-synonym tokens ' describes' and ' explains' (0.13/-0.04) in a plain expository frame: piece-specific hypothesis says silent, semantic rival says they should fire exactly like 'express'.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Officials said they would state their view at the meeting, and later tell reporters what the committee had decided after a long debate about the harbour.
adversarial_test_results.detail: ' said'/' state'/' tell' are the hypothesis's floor items (-0.17, -0.14, -0.04) in a reporting frame about putting a view into words, which the semantic rival treats as the pole's meaning.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: At the weekend the children make small paper boats and create clay figures for a model village that they keep on a shelf in the classroom.
adversarial_test_results.detail: ' make' (-0.09) and ' create' (0.15) are named floor pieces of the same 'bring into being' sense, so the hypothesis predicts silence while the semantic rival predicts firing.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The river cut a new form into the valley and changed the shape of the fields below the old mill, so the farmers had to invent a different way to reach the road.
adversarial_test_results.detail: ' form'/' shape'/' invent' are explicitly at the floor (0.07/0.06/-0.09) yet carry the bring-into-being meaning, and the to-infinitive 'to' ' reach' lets the syntactic rival predict firing too.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The building on the corner has four floors, and the buildings behind it have stood empty since the spring, when the last tenant moved out.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Missing inflections ' building' (0.14) and ' buildings' (-0.09) of a firing stem: hypothesis says silent, morphological rival says every derivative of the stem fires.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: My sister writes a page in her notebook every evening, and last week she wrote a long letter to her aunt about the garden.
adversarial_test_results.detail: ' writes' (0.02) and ' wrote' (0.08) are named floor inflections of the firing writing/written stem, separating piece-specificity from the morphological family reading.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The teacher spoke about education reform for an hour, and the educated parents in the room asked questions about the new rules for the school.
adversarial_test_results.detail: ' teacher' (0.07), ' education' (0.11) and ' educated' (0.08) are floor derivatives of firing teach/educate, so only the morphological rival predicts firing.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The delivery of the parts arrived two days late, and the combination of delays in the implementation of the new timetable meant the publication of the results slipped to June.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Four named floor derivatives (' delivery' 0.23, ' combination' 0.12, ' implementation' 0.07, ' publication' 0.08) crowd one sentence; the hypothesis predicts silence, the morphological rival firing.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The developer of the app said the developments of the last year had been hard to follow, and the client agreed to wait for the next update.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Floor derivatives ' developer' (0.30) and ' developments' (0.06) plus two to-infinitives ('to' ' follow', 'to' ' wait'), so hypothesis and syntactic rival predict opposite outcomes.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The protein sample sat in a cold buffer beside the enzyme, and the genome map on the bench showed where the sequence ended.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Every content noun is a named floor item (protein -0.09, sample -0.14, buffer -0.17, enzyme 0.11, genome -0.15), testing that the pole does not track scientific topic alone.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The regulation of information about pay, and the interpretation of the compensation rules, needed a special qualification from the board.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Five -ation nouns the hypothesis puts at the -0.17 floor (regulation, information, interpretation, compensation, qualification); all three rivals also predict silence, making this a plain control.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The state of the roads was poor, and as the saying goes a stitch in time saves nine, so the council said it would state a new plan in April.
adversarial_test_results.detail: ' state' as a noun and as a verb plus noun ' saying': the hypothesis's POS-invariance applies only to firing pieces, and the ' state' piece (state -0.14) is at the floor, while the semantic rival fires on the sense.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: An essay is a short piece of prose that a student hands in at the end of term. Most essays open with a claim, then give reasons and a few sources, and close with a short summary. The staff at most schools ask for a title page, a fixed margin and a list of sources at the back, and they mark the work against a set of rules listed in advance.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Long probe on the top examples' own topic (essays, student prose) that contains no firing piece at all, matching the long positive on token length while carrying none of the feature.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The phone call lasted nearly an hour, and after some discussion the group agreed to meet again in the spring to settle the last points before the deadline.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Communication-topic negative with no firing piece, carrying two to-infinitives ('to' ' meet', 'to' ' settle'), so the syntactic rival predicts firing while the hypothesis predicts silence.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Describe what you saw near the harbour last night, then tell the officer about the boat and the two men on the pier.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Sentence-initial capital 'Describe' splits into 'Des'+'cribe', neither of which is in the enumerated firing lexicon, and ' tell' (-0.04) is a floor piece, so the hypothesis predicts silence although the semantic rival reads the putting-into-words meaning.

adversarial_test_results.prompt:
Results:
The analysis of the sample shows a slow decline over the second half of the year, and the study team will meet on Friday to discuss it.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Negative opening on a colon and newline with floor ' analysis'/' sample'/' study' and a to-infinitive 'to' ' discuss', separating the piece claim from delimiter and frame effects.
Code genre with none of the claimed pieces, so no rival predicts firing; it checks that the pole is not a generic code or punctuation detector.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The price is twenty dollars, excluding tax and the delivery charge, and the shop will hold the item for one week.
adversarial_test_results.detail: ' excluding' is the piece-level opposite of the firing include family but is not a listed piece, and ' delivery' (0.23) is a named floor derivative, so hypothesis and morphological rival diverge.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The factory raised production last year and shipped more product to the coast, where a producer of tinned fish had opened a second plant.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Single-token derivatives of the firing produce stem that the hypothesis never lists (' production', ' product', ' producer') should sit at the floor, while the morphological rival expects them to fire.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The buyer shall pay the seller two hundred pounds within fourteen days of the date of this agreement, and the goods remain at the seller's risk until then.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Formal contract register with none of the claimed pieces, even though the scalar tail names 'formal' and 'explicit': hypothesis and all three rivals predict silence, a register control matched in length to the positives.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The express train to the coast left the station at seven, and the express lane on the motorway was clear all the way to the airport.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Two single-token ' express' pieces in adjective senses, the hypothesis's own confirmed 1.41 case, so the semantic rival (no putting-into-words meaning) and the syntactic rival are predicted wrong.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The water in the old tank was pure, and the syrup was so dense that the wooden spoon stood upright in it without help.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Scalar tail pieces ' pure' and ' dense' with no verbal sense at all: the hypothesis predicts firing, while all three rivals predict silence.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The nurse read the dose on the label, gave half a dose to the child, and noted the time on the chart beside the bed.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Technical-tail noun ' dose' twice, both single tokens, which the hypothesis says fires and the semantic rival explicitly dismisses as scan noise.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: For three days the villagers had watched the water rise, and by Thursday the bridge was gone. The elders met in the hall and argued about the road, and nobody could agree on a message. In the end they asked the schoolmaster to communicate the plan to the families downstream, one house at a time, before nightfall.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Long-context holdout with the single piece ' communicate' buried in a narrative, matched in length by the long essay negative, to test the claim that position in a passage is irrelevant.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Mix the flour with the yeast and a little warm water, cover the bowl with a cloth, and let the dough develop for an hour before shaping the loaves.
